name: Karlovy Vary
tagline: Bohemia's grandest 19th-century spa town, mineral hot springs wrapped in ornate colonnades beneath forested hills.
highlight: Sipping warm mineral water from a spa cup while strolling the Mill Colonnade's arcades, exactly as visitors have for two centuries.
shortDescription: Bohemia's grandest 19th-century spa town, its mineral hot springs framed by ornate colonnades, the Grandhotel Pupp and forested hills.
metaDescription: A Karlovy Vary travel guide: the Mill Colonnade, the Hot Spring Colonnade, Grandhotel Pupp, Becherovka, food and how to plan a spa town visit.
nearestAirport: Karlovy Vary Airport (KLV), or Václav Havel Airport Prague (PRG) about 2 hours by road
knownFor: Thermal spa colonnades, Grandhotel Pupp, Becherovka

image.alt: The Mill Colonnade in Karlovy Vary

intro: Karlovy Vary is Bohemia's grandest spa town, built up around a dozen mineral hot springs that have drawn visitors since the 14th century.
Its 19th-century golden age left behind an extraordinary collection of ornate colonnades and grand hotels, all set along the narrow Teplá River valley.
The town is still a working spa destination today, where sipping mineral water from a distinctive spa cup remains as central to a visit as any sightseeing.

whyVisit.intro: Karlovy Vary's case rests on extraordinary spa-town architecture paired with a still-living thermal spa tradition.

points.title: The colonnades are architectural showpieces
points.text: Ornate 19th-century ironwork and stone arcades built specifically to frame the mineral springs.

points.title: The springs are still in daily use
points.text: A centuries-old tradition of sipping warm mineral water from a spa cup continues today.

points.title: The setting is beautiful
points.text: A narrow river valley wrapped in forested hills, with a funicular up to a hilltop lookout.

points.title: It's home to Becherovka
points.text: The town's own herbal liqueur, distilled here since 1807.

points.title: It works well as a change of pace from Prague
points.text: A relaxed, unhurried spa-town atmosphere quite different from the capital.

attractionsIntro: Karlovy Vary's essential sights are its colonnades, grand hotels and the springs themselves.

attractions.name: The Mill Colonnade

image.alt: The Mill Colonnade in Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: The town's largest and grandest colonnade, a neo-Renaissance arcade covering five separate mineral springs.
attractions.tip: Bring or buy a spa cup here to sample the water as you walk.

attractions.name: The Hot Spring Colonnade

image.alt: The Hot Spring Colonnade in Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: Home to the town's hottest and most powerful spring, shooting water up to 12 metres into the air.
attractions.tip: The modern glass building looks stark from outside, but the spring itself is impressive.

attractions.name: Grandhotel Pupp

image.alt: The historic Grandhotel Pupp in Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: The town's grandest hotel since 1701, and a regular filming location for international movies.
attractions.tip: Stop for a coffee in the lobby even if you're not staying — it's open to non-guests.

attractions.name: The Diana Lookout Tower

image.file: File:Karlovy Vary, horní stanice lanové dráhy Diana a rozhledna.jpg
image.alt: The Diana Lookout Tower above Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: The best view over the town, an observation tower reached by a short funicular ride.
attractions.tip: Walk back down through the forest instead of taking the funicular both ways.

attractions.name: Church of St Mary Magdalene

image.file: File:Church of Saint Mary Magdalene (Karlovy Vary).JPG
image.alt: The Church of St Mary Magdalene in Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: The town's baroque parish church, designed by the same architect behind Prague's St Nicholas Church.
attractions.tip: Visible from most of the colonnade district, an easy landmark to navigate by.

attractions.name: The Market Colonnade

image.file: File:Fountain near the Market Colonnade. Karlovy Vary, Czech Republic.jpg
image.alt: The Market Colonnade in Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: A delicate white wooden colonnade, among the most photogenic in town.
attractions.tip: A lovely spot in the late afternoon light, just up the valley from the Mill Colonnade.

attractions.name: The Jan Becher Museum

image.alt: The Jan Becher Museum in Karlovy Vary

attractions.text: The home of Becherovka, the town's herbal liqueur distilled here since 1807.
attractions.tip: Book the tour, which ends with a tasting of several Becherovka varieties.

thingsToDoIntro: Karlovy Vary rewards an unhurried pace, built around its springs, colonnades and forested hills.

thingsToDo.title: Sip mineral water from a spa cup

image.alt: Sipping mineral water at a colonnade in Karlovy Vary

thingsToDo.text: An essential Karlovy Vary ritual, strolling between colonnades sampling different mineral springs.
thingsToDo.tip: Buy a spa cup with a built-in straw from any souvenir shop — the water is often too hot to sip normally.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the funicular to the Diana Lookout Tower

image.file: File:Karlovy Vary stanice lanovky Jelení skok (04).jpg
image.alt: A viewpoint above Karlovy Vary

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding short trip, climbing above the colonnades for a sweeping view over the town.
thingsToDo.tip: Go late afternoon for the best light over the valley.

thingsToDo.title: Tour the Jan Becher Museum and taste Becherovka

image.alt: Becherovka, a herbal liqueur from Karlovy Vary

thingsToDo.text: A worthwhile hour, learning the story behind the town's own herbal liqueur before a tasting.
thingsToDo.tip: Pick up a bottle at the museum shop — it's a classic, packable Karlovy Vary souvenir.

thingsToDo.title: Buy a spa wafer (lázeňské oplatky)

image.alt: Traditional spa wafers, a Karlovy Vary specialty

thingsToDo.text: A traditional pairing, thin sweet wafers sold specifically to eat alongside the mineral water.
thingsToDo.tip: Try a few different flavours from one of the colonnade kiosks.

thingsToDo.title: Have a drink at the Grandhotel Pupp

image.alt: The historic Grandhotel Pupp in Karlovy Vary

thingsToDo.text: An elegant way to spend an hour, taking in the hotel's grand historic interiors over a coffee or drink.
thingsToDo.tip: The terrace is a lovely spot to sit in warmer months.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the Market Colonnade

image.file: File:Karlovy Vary, Vřídelní kolonáda od zámku.JPG
image.alt: A colonnade in Karlovy Vary

thingsToDo.text: A photogenic stop, the delicate white woodwork among the prettiest in town.
thingsToDo.tip: Visit early morning for photos without other visitors in frame.

foodIntro: Karlovy Vary's food centres on its spa traditions alongside standard Czech classics.

foods.name: Lázeňské oplatky (spa wafers)

image.alt: Traditional Czech spa wafers

foods.text: The town's signature treat, thin sweet wafers traditionally eaten alongside the mineral water.
foods.whereToTry: Colonnade kiosks and bakeries throughout the spa district.

foods.name: Becherovka

image.alt: A bottle of Becherovka herbal liqueur

foods.text: The town's own herbal liqueur, distilled here since 1807 and often served as a digestif.
foods.whereToTry: Bars and restaurants throughout Karlovy Vary, or the Jan Becher Museum itself.

foods.name: Svíčková (marinated beef in cream sauce)

image.alt: Svíčková, marinated beef in cream sauce with bread dumplings

foods.text: A reliable classic, found at traditional restaurants throughout town.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants around the colonnade district.

foods.name: Guláš with dumplings

image.alt: Czech goulash served with bread dumplings

foods.text: A warming option away from the colonnades' more tourist-focused cafés.
foods.whereToTry: Local pubs slightly outside the main spa district.

foods.name: Czech beer (pivo)

image.alt: A glass of Czech pilsner beer

foods.text: A good counterpoint to a day of mineral water, though this is first and foremost a spa town.
foods.whereToTry: Pubs a short walk from the main colonnade district.

foods.name: Smažený sýr (fried cheese)

image.file: File:Smažený sýr s tatarskou omáčkou a brambory.jpg
image.alt: Smažený sýr, breaded fried cheese with tartar sauce and potatoes

foods.text: A satisfying, inexpensive option away from the spa district's pricier cafés.
foods.whereToTry: Local restaurants slightly outside the colonnade area.

accommodation.intro: Karlovy Vary offers everything from grand historic hotels to simpler guesthouses just outside the spa core.

areas.bestFor: Being steps from every major spa sight
areas.text: Historic hotels right along the Teplá River, including the famous Grandhotel Pupp.

areas.name: Just outside the spa core

areas.text: Simpler guesthouses within easy walking distance of the main sights.

gettingThere.intro: Karlovy Vary is an easy trip from Prague, whether as a day trip or overnight stay.

options.text: The easiest and fastest option, taking about two hours.
options.detail: Frequent daily services run from Prague's main bus terminals.

options.text: A scenic alternative, taking slightly longer than the bus.
options.detail: Around three hours, with pleasant countryside views along the way.

options.text: Convenient for a rushed visit without your own transport.
options.detail: Widely available from Prague hotels and tour operators.

gettingAround.intro: Karlovy Vary's compact spa core is entirely walkable, with a funicular for the surrounding hills.

options.text: The only way to properly experience the colonnades.
options.detail: The spa district's main sights all sit within an easy walk of each other.

options.text: The easiest way up to the best viewpoint over town.
options.detail: A short, inexpensive ride from near the Grandhotel Pupp.

options.mode: Local bus from the train station
options.text: Useful, as the station sits a little outside the spa core.
options.detail: A short ride connects the station to the colonnade district.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for pleasant walking weather
bestTime.summary: Karlovy Vary is a year-round spa destination, with the indoor springs open regardless of season.

seasons.text: Mild, comfortable weather for strolling between colonnades.
Warm and busy, especially during the town's film festival in early July.
Golden light over the forested valley, with thinner crowds than summer.
Atmospheric with the warm colonnades a cosy contrast to the cold outside.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly, though early July's film festival fills hotels well ahead.

itinerary.title: One day in Karlovy Vary
itinerary.intro: A single full day covering the colonnades, a lookout tower and the Becherovka museum.

days.title: The colonnades and Diana Tower
days.summary: A full day of springs, architecture and views.
days.morning: The Mill and Hot Spring Colonnades, spa cup in hand.
days.afternoon: The Jan Becher Museum, then the funicular to Diana Lookout Tower.
days.evening: A drink at the Grandhotel Pupp before dinner.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Karlovy Vary visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Buy a spa cup from any souvenir shop before trying the mineral springs.
Book the Jan Becher Museum tour ahead in peak season.
Pack comfortable shoes — the funicular walk back down covers some distance.
Try more than one spring — each one tastes noticeably different.
Visit as a day trip or add one night — a single day covers the essentials well.
Book well ahead for early July, when the town's film festival fills every hotel.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Karlovy Vary?
faq.a: One full day covers the essential colonnades and a lookout tower; an overnight stay allows a more relaxed pace.

faq.q: Can you actually drink the spa water?
faq.a: Yes — it's intended for drinking, traditionally sipped from a spa cup while walking between colonnades.

faq.q: Is Karlovy Vary worth visiting from Prague?
faq.a: Yes — its 19th-century spa architecture and thermal springs are unlike anything in the capital.

faq.q: How do you get from Prague to Karlovy Vary?
faq.a: Easiest by direct bus, taking about two hours; the train is a scenic alternative taking slightly longer.
Karlovy Vary's own herbal liqueur, distilled here since 1807 and still produced in the town today.

faq.q: Is Karlovy Vary a day trip or worth staying overnight?
faq.a: Both work — a day trip covers the highlights, while staying overnight allows a properly unhurried spa-town pace.
